Read section 94 in three witnesses: the archive.org OCR of the Macmillan scan (title page THE MACMILLAN COMPANY 1907, introduction dated August 1907), the 1909 scan, and Gutenberg 4363. All three read “The maturity of man—that means, to have reacquired the seriousness that one had as a child at play.”, the whole aphorism, numbered 94, under FOURTH CHAPTER. APOPHTHEGMS AND INTERLUDES. So the wording is Zimmern’s, not Kaufmann’s (“Man’s maturity: to have regained the seriousness that he had as a child at play”) or Hollingdale’s, and the correction of the date to 1907 is sound.
